title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: 'precise/absolute elect cannot be commanded to believe' misreads absolute election as cutting off means
latin: Porro quod in argumento positum fuit, Precise sive absolute electis aut reprobis non posse mandari ut credant, si eo sensu accipiunt precise et absolute ad salutem electos, ut praescindant ab usu mediorum, quasi Deus decrevisset aliquos ad salutem perducere etiamsi media salutis rejiciant, aut aliquos damnare, etiamsi in Christum crediderint, pro nostro dogmate sua insomnia obtrudunt.
pass_a: Further, what was put in the argument, that it cannot be commanded unto the precisely or absolutely elect or reprobate that they believe, if in that sense they take those precisely and absolutely elected unto salvation so as to cut them off from the use of means, as if God had decreed to bring some unto salvation even if they reject the means of salvation, or to damn some even if they shall have believed in Christ, they thrust their own dreams upon us for our dogma.
pass_b: They also put it that the precisely or absolutely elect or reprobate cannot be commanded to believe. Take that in their sense of people elected to salvation so precisely that means drop out — as if God had decreed to bring some to salvation even though they reject every means of it, or to damn some even though they believe in Christ. That is not our dogma. It is their dream forced onto ours.

lemmas.gloss: adversaries misread absolute election as means-free
they foist dreams on our dogma

title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: Peter and Paul absolutely predestined to life and to the whole series of means — will of end absolutely joined to will of means
latin: Nos dicimus, Petrum, Paulum, reliquosque ad vitam aeternam absolute praedestinatos, non quod ipsi antequam credant absolute sciant hoc Dei decretum, aut quod ipsi vitam aeternam consequantur fidei conditione minime praestita; sed quod a Deo absolute et gratuito eliguntur, non modo ad ipsam vitam aeternam, sed ad totam seriem mediorum quibus ad eam perducuntur. Licet itaque in exsecutione finis pendeat a conditionali usu mediorum, tamen in Deo praedestinante Petrum, Paulum, aut quamcunque personam singularem, voluntas finis non fuit conditionata, sed absolute connexa cum voluntate mediorum; ita ut uno et eodem simplicissimo actu, quo Deus voluit Petro aut Paulo gloriam, voluerit etiam et fidem, ceteraque omnia ex quorum usu conditionali gloria promittitur. Uno verbo, Deus non decrevit servare Petrum sine conditione fidei, sed tam absolute et precise fidem Petro dare decrevit, quam salutem. Atque hoc est quod vulgo dicitur, Praedestinationem esse praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro.
pass_a: We say that Peter, Paul, and the rest are absolutely predestined unto eternal life, not that they themselves before they believe absolutely know this decree of God, or that they themselves obtain eternal life the condition of faith being in no wise performed; but that they are elected by God absolutely and gratuitously, not only unto eternal life itself, but unto the whole series of means by which they are brought unto it. Although therefore in the execution of the end it hangs upon the conditional use of means, yet in God predestinating Peter, Paul, or any singular person, the will of the end was not conditioned, but absolutely connected with the will of the means; so that by one and the same most simple act by which God willed glory unto Peter or Paul, he also willed faith, and all the rest from whose conditional use glory is promised. In a word, God did not decree to save Peter without the condition of faith, but as absolutely and precisely decreed to give faith unto Peter as salvation. And this is what is commonly said, that Predestination is the preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future.
pass_b: We say Peter, Paul, and the rest are absolutely predestined to eternal life — not that they know that decree absolutely before they believe, or that they gain eternal life with the faith-condition never performed — but that God elects them absolutely and freely not only to eternal life itself but to the whole series of means by which they are brought to it. In execution the end hangs on conditional use of means; yet in God predestining Peter, Paul, or any particular person, the will of the end was not conditioned but absolutely joined to the will of the means — so that by one and the same simplest act by which God willed glory for Peter or Paul he also willed faith and all else from whose conditional use glory is promised. In a word: God did not decree to save Peter without the condition of faith, but decreed to give Peter faith as absolutely and precisely as salvation. That is the common saying: Predestination is preparation of grace now and of glory hereafter.

lemmas.gloss: absolute election includes whole series of means
will of end absolutely connected with will of means

title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: reprobates may be commanded to believe and offered salvation if they believe — as non-elect angels were commanded to obey
latin: Jam quod attinet ad reprobatos, non obstante aeterna antecedanea reprobatione, tam potest iis mandari ut credant, quam potuit vere mandari Angelis non-electis sive reprobatis ut obediant Deo: tam potest iis offerri salus sub conditione, Si credant, quam potuit his promitti beatitudo sub conditione, Si in obsequio Dei perseverassent. Nam ut praedestinatio Petri non tollit veritatem hujus negativae conditionalis, Si non credideris, non salvaberis: ita reprobatio Judae non enervat veritatem hujus affirmativae conditionalis, Si tu credideris, tu salvaberis: sed infert solummodo, stante indissolubili illa conditionali fidei et salutis concatenatione, non dandam eam efficacem gratiam Judae, qua de facto conditionem impleat.
pass_a: Now as to what pertains unto the reprobate, eternal antecedent reprobation notwithstanding, it can as well be commanded unto them that they believe, as it could truly be commanded unto the non-elect or reprobate Angels that they obey God: salvation can as well be offered unto them under the condition, If they believe, as beatitude could be promised unto those under the condition, If they had persevered in the obedience of God. For as the predestination of Peter does not take away the truth of this negative conditional, If thou shalt not have believed, thou shalt not be saved: so the reprobation of Judas does not enervate the truth of this affirmative conditional, If thou shalt have believed, thou shalt be saved: but infers only, that indissoluble conditional concatenation of faith and salvation standing, that efficacious grace is not to be given unto Judas by which he would in fact fulfill the condition.
pass_b: As for the reprobate: eternal antecedent reprobation notwithstanding, they can as truly be commanded to believe as the non-elect or reprobate angels could be commanded to obey God; salvation can as truly be offered them on the condition If they believe as beatitude could be promised those angels on If they had persevered in God's obedience. Peter's predestination does not cancel the truth of If you do not believe, you will not be saved; Judas's reprobation does not weaken If you believe, you will be saved. It only implies that, that indissoluble faith-salvation bond standing, Judas is not to be given the efficacious grace by which he would in fact fulfill the condition.

lemmas.gloss: reprobates may be commanded to believe
conditional promise true for Judas too

title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: reprobates are not required to believe a falsehood — Christ's death applies under the revealed condition of faith, not secret predestination (John 3:15–16)
latin: Denique, quod objectum fuit, ex sententia nostra a reprobatis exigi ut falsum credant, scilicet Christum morte sua illis vitam et reconciliationem impetrasse, plane negatur. Vita enim et reconciliatio per mortem Christi non impetratur singularibus hominibus applicanda sub conditione hac arcana, Si fuerint praedestinati, sed sub conditione revelata, si fuerint fideles; neque negatur applicanda ulli singulari personae cui praedicatur, nisi sub hac conditione, si fuerit infidelis, ut aperte colligitur Joan. iii. 15, 16, etc. In hoc igitur se exserit arcanum illud electionis et reprobationis decretum, quod mors Christi, quae ex ordinatione Dei cuivis homini, si crederet, ad reconciliationem et vitam obtinendam valeret, non proficit tamen nisi electis, quibus solis ex speciali misericordia datur illa gratia, qua efficaciter possint et velint, et reapse adimpleant dictam conditionem.
pass_a: Finally, what was objected, that on our sentence it is exacted of the reprobate that they believe a falsehood, namely that Christ by his death obtained life and reconciliation for them, is plainly denied. For life and reconciliation through the death of Christ is not obtained to be applied unto singular men under this secret condition, If they shall have been predestined, but under the revealed condition, if they shall have been faithful; nor is it denied to be applied unto any singular person unto whom it is preached, except under this condition, if he shall have been unfaithful, as is openly gathered from John iii. 15, 16, etc. In this therefore that secret decree of election and reprobation puts itself forth, that the death of Christ, which by the ordination of God would avail unto any man, if he believed, unto obtaining reconciliation and life, yet profits only the elect, unto whom alone from special mercy is given that grace by which they can and will efficaciously, and in fact fulfill, the said condition.
pass_b: Finally, the objection that on our view the reprobate are required to believe a falsehood — that Christ by his death obtained life and reconciliation for them — is plainly denied. Life and reconciliation through Christ's death are not applied to particulars under the secret condition If they were predestined, but under the revealed condition if they are believers; nor is application denied to any hearer except under if he is an unbeliever — as John 3:15–16 openly shows. Here the secret election/reprobation decree shows itself: Christ's death, which by God's ordination would avail any man who believed for reconciliation and life, yet profits only the elect, to whom alone from special mercy is given that grace by which they can and will efficaciously, and in fact, fulfill that condition.

lemmas.gloss: application under revealed faith-condition, not secret predestination

title: Cap. IX Arg. 6 open: absolute reprobation not from foresight of final impenitence is said to cast perdition's cause on defect of grace — Corvinus
latin: Qui ponunt reprobationem absolutam et non ex praevisione finalis impoenitentiae ortam, illi causam perditionis rejiciunt non in propriam ipsorum reprobatorum malitiam, sed in gratiae Divinae defectum: At hoc nimis Deo indignum, qui semper paratus est gratiam ulteriorem addere, si homo bene utatur accepta: Non igitur ex reprobatione, sed ex voluntaria hominis neglectu accidit, quod gratia careat, aut quod majorem non accipiat, nimirum quod sese vita aeterna reddiderit indignum, Act. xiii. 46. quod veritatem in injustitia detinuerit, Rom. i. 18. quod non receperit amorem veritatis, 2 Thess. ii. 10, 11.
pass_a: They who place absolute reprobation and not sprung from foresight of final impenitence, those cast the cause of perdition not upon the reprobates' own malice, but upon defect of Divine grace: But this is too unworthy of God, who is always prepared to add further grace, if a man well use what is received: Therefore not from reprobation, but from the voluntary neglect of man it comes to pass that he lacks grace, or that he does not receive greater, namely that he has rendered himself unworthy of eternal life, Acts xiii. 46. that he has held the truth in unrighteousness, Rom. i. 18. that he has not received the love of the truth, 2 Thess. ii. 10, 11.
pass_b: Those who set absolute reprobation not sprung from foresight of final impenitence cast perdition's cause not on the reprobates' own malice but on a defect of divine grace. That, they say, is too unworthy of God, who is always ready to add further grace if a man uses well what he has received. So not from reprobation but from a man's voluntary neglect it comes that he lacks grace or does not receive more — namely that he has made himself unworthy of eternal life (Acts 13:46), held the truth in unrighteousness (Rom. 1:18), and not received the love of the truth (2 Thess. 2:10–11).

lemmas.gloss: adversaries: absolute reprobation blames defect of grace

lemmas.lemma: Act. xiii. 46 / Rom. i. 18 / 2 Thess. ii.

title: Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol open: reprobation does not make God or defect of grace the true cause of human perdition — the sinner with his sins is the true and sole cause
latin: Negamus, ex reprobatione a nobis posita aut Deum ipsum constitui causam perditionis humanae, aut Divinae gratiae defectum, nisi causa vocabulum improprie et abusive usurpetur. Perditionis enim sive damnationis vera causa est illud quod damnationem juste meretur, vel ille qui damnatione digna operatur. Sic ipse peccator cum peccatis suis est sibi vera et sola causa perditionis suae. Esse enim reprobatum, vel a gratiae ac misericordiae specialis praeparatione praeteritum, nec meretur nec operatur perditionem. Illa igitur quam docemus non rejicit causam damnationis in Divinae gratiae defectum, sed revera rejicit efficacis et specialis gratiae negationem in Divinae voluntatis libertatem. Dei voluntas causa est determinans, quod quidam per gratiam efficacem et infrustrabilem non eruantur ex perditione, aliis per talem gratiam erutis; sed propria reprobatorum malitia causa est operativa et meritoria cur perdantur et damnentur.
pass_a: We deny that from the reprobation posited by us either God himself is constituted the cause of human perdition, or a defect of Divine grace, unless the word cause be used improperly and abusively. For the true cause of perdition or damnation is that which justly deserves damnation, or he who works things worthy of damnation. So the sinner himself with his sins is unto himself the true and sole cause of his perdition. For to be reprobated, or passed by from the preparation of special grace and mercy, neither deserves nor works perdition. That therefore which we teach does not cast the cause of damnation upon a defect of Divine grace, but in truth casts the negation of efficacious and special grace upon the liberty of the Divine will. The will of God is the determining cause that certain ones are not drawn out of perdition by efficacious and unfrustrable grace, others being drawn out by such grace; but the reprobates' own malice is the operative and meritorious cause why they perish and are damned.
pass_b: We deny that the reprobation we teach makes God himself — or a defect of divine grace — the cause of human perdition, unless 'cause' is used improperly and abusively. The true cause of perdition or damnation is what justly deserves damnation, or the one who works what damnation is due. So the sinner himself with his sins is to himself the true and sole cause of his perdition. Being reprobated, or passed by from preparation of special grace and mercy, neither deserves nor works perdition. What we teach does not cast damnation's cause on a defect of divine grace; it casts the denial of efficacious special grace on the liberty of divine will. God's will is the determining cause that some are not drawn out of perdition by efficacious unfrustrable grace while others are; the reprobates' own malice is the operative meritorious cause why they perish and are damned.

lemmas.gloss: sinner with sins is true sole cause of perdition
reprobates' malice operative/meritorious; God's will determining
